content.title: Shodōe
about: Shodōe is a dark first-person roguelike deckbuilder set in a surreal feudal-Japan-inspired world filled with yokai.

The core mechanic turns cards into physical cutting patterns: instead of dealing abstract damage, players place geometric shapes over an enemy and use them to sever limbs, isolate vital parts, and solve each combat as an anatomical puzzle.
Developed by SouthWest Studio as a CITM pre-incubator beta prototype, focused on validating the tension, discovery, and precision of its card-cutting combat loop.
features: Tactical turn-based combat built around cards, ink management, and precise geometric cuts
Enemy anatomy system where severing limbs, revealing weak points, and isolating hearts determines the outcome of combat
Branching roguelike map with combat rooms, shops, sacrifice altars, fusion altars, upgrade rooms, and a boss encounter
Card effects such as Fantasmal, Reveal, and Combustion, plus upgrade, fusion, sacrifice, and death-card progression systems
Rail-based first-person exploration with camera transitions for combat, shops, altars, and path selection
Diegetic UI, tutorial flow, dialogue systems, bestiary/settings panels, and extensive polish for the beta release
learnings: Designing combat systems where spatial precision and enemy anatomy replace traditional damage numbers
Building procedural map generation with constrained branching, room weights, and route validation
Connecting logical map nodes to first-person rail movement, room spawning, corridors, and camera transitions
Integrating many interconnected card systems: effects, fusion, upgrades, sacrifice, shop generation, and death-card persistence
Polishing a beta prototype through UI/settings work, tutorials, dialogue flow, boss fixes, build stability, and release preparation
